title: lore impact: usage and machine manifest don't mark --direction as required
description:
Usage is 'lore impact <id>' and the flag list does not identify --direction as required. 'lore impact PGF-3 --kind task --json' exits 2 with '--direction is required'. Adding --direction outbound succeeds, and the documented example does carry one -- so the requirement exists and is correct, it's just invisible until the command fails.

Help usability, not a graph correctness bug -- but the machine-manifest half matters more than it looks, since that is what an agent reads to construct a valid invocation without trial-and-error.

Fix: show the requirement in usage, and expose required flags in the machine manifest (lore's --json manifest / help output), or give --direction a documented default.

Source: 2026-09-13 proof-graph inspection (Lore 0.6.0, Quest 0.6.0), read-only against production, recorded as OPAG-120 on opum-agent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore impact's usage/help output shows --direction as required, not merely present in an example
The machine-readable manifest (lore manifest --json or equivalent) marks --direction as a required flag for the impact command
A regression test asserts the manifest's required-flag metadata for the impact command, or --direction gets a documented default and the required-flag error is removed
